question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 100 cm and one of the diagonals is 40 cm. Then the area of the rhombus is
solution:
**Given:**

Perimeter of the rhombus = 100 cm

One diagonal = 40 cm

**Formula used:**

Perimeter of rhombus = 4 × side

Area of the rhombus = (1/2) × diagonal₁ × diagonal₂

**Calculation:**

⇒ Side of the rhombus = Perimeter / 4 = 100 / 4 = 25 cm

Now, let the second diagonal be d₂.

By the Pythagorean theorem, the diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. So, each half of the diagonals forms a right-angled triangle.

⇒ (half of diagonal₁)² + (half of diagonal₂)² = side²

⇒ (40/2)² + (d₂/2)² = 25²

⇒ 20² + (d₂/2)² = 625

⇒ 400 + (d₂/2)² = 625

⇒ (d₂/2)² = 625 - 400 = 225

⇒ d₂/2 = 15

⇒ d₂ = 30 cm

⇒ Area = (1/2) × diagonal₁ × diagonal₂

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 40 × 30

⇒ Area = 600 cm²

**∴ The area of the rhombus is 600 cm².**
